arguments.content:
# Pilot CLI Documentation

## Case Selection

The `--case` flag allows selecting specific test cases to run from the suite.

### Usage Example

```bash
pilot --case alpha --case gamma
```

This command runs only the `alpha` and `gamma` cases.

### Behavior Details

- Repeated `--case` flags select each named case once, preserving the original suite order.
- Duplicate case IDs in the flags are ignored; each case runs only once.
- If no `--case` flags are provided, all cases run by default (no filtering).
- Unknown case IDs cause an immediate error before any output or execution.
- The output directory must not already exist to prevent overwriting previous results.

This behavior ensures precise control over which cases run, while maintaining safety and reproducibility.

## Usage

By default, all cases in the suite are executed in their original order.

To run only specific cases, use the `--case` flag one or more times. The order of execution follows the original suite order, and duplicate flags are ignored.

Example: run only the `alpha` and `gamma` cases in suite order:

```bash
python scripts/run_coupled_pilot.py \
  --binary ./target/debug/coupled-pilot \
  --repo . \
  --out ./out \
  --provider openai \
  --model gpt-4o-mini \
  --case alpha \
  --case gamma
```

Notes:
- Repeated `--case` flags are deduplicated; each case runs once in original suite order.
- Unknown case IDs are rejected before any output or execution.
- Omitting `--case` runs all cases in suite order.
